A.explanation: This is about 100 times too small and results from leaving the length as $12$ in centimetres instead of $0.12\text{ m}$ in $I = Ne v / L$.

B.explanation: This is far too small for $5.1 \times 10^{22}$ electrons drifting together and comes from mishandling powers of ten or the length conversion.

C.explanation: Using $I = Ne v / L$ with $N = 5.1 \times 10^{22}$, $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$, $v = 4.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $L = 0.12\text{ m}$ gives about $0.27\text{ A}$.

D.explanation: This is larger than the correct value and can come from an arithmetic slip with $N$, $e$, $v$ and $L$, for example incorrect combination of the powers of ten.

hints: Notice the question gives the total number of free electrons $N = 5.1 \times 10^{22}$ in the whole $12\text{ cm}$ wire, not the number density $n$, plus the drift speed $4.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Recall current is charge passing per unit time, so combine $I = nAvq$ with $N = nAL$ to get $I = N e v / L$ for the total charge $Ne$ in length $L$.

Convert $12\text{ cm}$ to $0.12\text{ m}$, use $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$, then evaluate $(5.1 \times 10^{22})(1.60 \times 10^{-19})(4.0 \times 10^{-6}) / 0.12$ and check the unit is $\text{A}$.
walkthrough: Identify the total mobile charge: the wire contains $N = 5.1 \times 10^{22}$ free electrons, each of charge $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$, so total charge is $Q = Ne$.
Relate drift to current: in time $t$ an electron drifts distance $v t$, so the fraction of the wire length $L$ emptied per unit time is $v/L$, giving $I = Q/t = Ne v / L$.
Convert length to SI units: $L = 12\text{ cm} = 0.12\text{ m}$, while $v = 4.0 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is already in SI units.

Work stepwise: $(5.1 \times 10^{22})(1.60 \times 10^{-19}) = 8.16 \times 10^{3}$, then $8.16 \times 10^{3} \times 4.0 \times 10^{-6} = 3.264 \times 10^{-2}$, then division by $0.12$ gives about $0.27\text{ A}$.
The unit is coulombs per second, i.e. amperes, and the value matches $0.27\text{ A}$. This is option C.
